title: Loquitur reason code description catalog
description: Catalog of human-readable descriptions for loquitur.reason_codes.v1. Each entry maps a machine-readable reason code to deterministic, audience-specific narrative content for the verdict explainability layer (the versioned reason-code catalog).

catalog_version.description: Semantic version of this catalog. Bumps when wording changes; new entries are minor; removed entries are major.

reason_code_vocabulary.description: Pinned to the reason code vocabulary this catalog describes. Catalog must be re-issued for any new vocabulary version.

audiences.description: The fixed audience sequence, in this exact order. Order is contract here, not presentation: the reference loader compares positionally (tuple(audiences) != CATALOG_AUDIENCES), so a set-shaped constraint would accept a catalog the reference implementation rejects: ['executive','technical','compliance'] would validate and then fail to load. Adding a new audience is a major version bump.

entries.description: Map of reason code identifier to its catalog entry. The key pattern is the whole of what this schema checks, and deliberately so: this file is where loquitur.reason_codes.v1 is defined, so closing the keys over the vocabulary here would mean a second hand-maintained copy of every code inside the file that defines them -- a second copy of a value, which can drift from the first. Key parity with the published enums, and the absence of gaps, are gated by test instead: tests/test_reason_code_vocabulary_self_contained.py and tests/test_verdict_grounds.py of loquitur-schemas both fail on an entries map that is empty or missing a published code.

composition_templates.description: Audience-specific verdict lead and closing templates used by deterministic narrative renderers. These templates keep reason-code catalog wording as the single source of truth instead of duplicating business-critical prose in verifier code.

code.description: Reason code identifier. It must equal the map key and JSON Schema cannot say so -- no keyword binds a value to its parent's property name -- so the equality is gated in loquitur-schemas, tests/test_reason_codes_catalog.py::test_every_entry_code_matches_map_key. The pattern is all this schema can assert.

category.description: The category of the entry. The name anchoring is reserved for method-neutral anchoring codes and is not a category of this version (reason-codes.md section 3).

headline.description: Single-sentence technical summary in neutral voice.

detail.description: Composed paragraph for engineers. Vocabulary may include canonicalization, hash, RFC references, schema names. Neutral imperative voice for actions.

consequence.description: Composed paragraph naming the operational impact. Must be assertive (must / cannot / do not), never softened (should consider / may want to).

required_action.description: Specific action required of the bundle producer or downstream consumer. Imperative voice.

summary.description: Short summary in non-technical assertive voice -- two or three sentences where the outcome needs them, one where it does not; eleven of the shipped entries are a single sentence, so this is editorial intent rather than a rule. No jargon, no hash references, no RFC citations. Stake the operational outcome plainly.
